findings.issue_text: [Medium/performance] pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — after acquiring the write lock, entryPointAssetsCache is not re-checked, so concurrent first non-dev callers that saw nil each reload and parse the manifest instead of reusing the first result.

[Medium/performance] pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48-70 — the exclusive lock is held during manifest reading/parsing and possible CDN requests, unnecessarily serializing concurrent dev-mode requests that bypass the cache.

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48-70 — the exclusive lock is held during manifest reading/parsing and possible CDN requests, unnecessarily serializing concurrent dev-mode requests that bypass the cache.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that after the RLock check, the code acquires an exclusive Lock (line 48) and holds it with 'defer Unlock()' through the rest of the function (lines 48-70 based on the diff context). In dev mode where cfg.Env == setting.Dev, the cache is bypassed (ret check fails), so every request will acquire the exclusive lock and hold it during manifest reading/parsing operations. This is a valid performance concern about the implementation approach, though it's architectural feedback rather than a bug since the code is functionally correct.
